q: 151. The capacity of septic tank for 100 users will be roughly
explain: For a small number of users (around 10), a septic tank typically requires a capacity of about 7 to 8 cubic meters to allow for proper sedimentation and sludge storage.

q: 152. In a galvanised corrugated iron sheet the pitch (centre to centre distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: The standard pitch for CGI (Corrugated Galvanized Iron) sheets used in roofing is generally 75 mm (3 inches).

q: 153. Besides standard length and width of a corrugated sheet, one important dimension usually considered is
explain: The gauge (thickness) of the material is a critical dimension as it determines the strength, durability, and weight of the corrugated sheet.

q: 154. Which one of the following is not the standard length of asbestos cement corrugated sheets
explain: Standard lengths for AC sheets usually come in increments like 1.5m, 2.0m, 1.75m, and 3.0m; 2.5m is not considered a standard manufacturing length.

q: 155. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A expenditure-receipt statement is a formal statement of estimated income and expenses for a specific future period, usually one year.

q: 156. A work costing less than Rs. 20000 is termed as
explain: In many public works departments, works are categorized by cost; works costing between a few thousand up to 20,000 (or 50,000 depending on specific local norms) are often classified as petty Works.

q: 157. A work costing more than Rs. one core is termed as
explain: High-value projects (typically exceeding a specific threshold like 1 Crore) are classified as Major Works requiring higher-level technical and administrative sanction.

q: 158. The unit of measurement of brick work in foundation is
explain: General brickwork in foundations and superstructures is measured by volume in cubic meters (m³).

q: 159. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S : 1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: The cross-sectional area consists of a central rectangle (B × d) and two side triangles (each 1/2 × Sd × d), totaling Bd + Sd².

q: 160. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: All these methods (Mid-section, Trapezoidal/Mean-sectional, and Prismoidal) are valid mathematical approaches to calculate earthwork volumes for road construction.

q: 161. Estimate is
options: the actual cost of construction of a structure
the probable cost arrived at before commencement of the structure
a random guess of the cost of the structure
explain: An estimate is a technical calculation of the probable cost of a project, prepared before the work starts based on drawings and specifications.

q: 162. Which of the following is the most correct estimate?
explain: A detailed estimate is the most accurate because it calculates the quantity of every individual item of work based on actual dimensions.

q: 163. In absence of detailed design the percentage of steel in concrete columns is usually taken as
explain: For preliminary estimation, the reinforcement in columns is generally assumed to be between 1% and 5% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 164. The unit of measurement of form work
explain: Formwork (shuttering and centering) is measured by the area of the surface in contact with the concrete, expressed in square meters (m²).

q: 165. The unit of measurement of striking is
explain: 'Striking' refers to the removal of formwork, and like the installation, it is measured based on the area (m²).

q: 166. The unit of measurement of supply of urinals; commode, trap basin etc is
explain: Sanitary fittings like urinals, commodes, and basins are counted and paid for by the number of units (no.).

q: 167. The unit of measurement of masonry work (ashlar and rubble) is
explain: Stone masonry, whether ashlar (dressed) or rubble (undressed), is a volumetric item measured in cubic meters (m³).

q: 168. A fixed stated sum of penalty to help by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-estimated sum agreed upon in the contract to be paid if the contractor fails to complete the work on time.

q: 169. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Items like rolling shutters and steel doors are typically measured by their clear area in square meters (m²).

q: 170. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measures in sq. m
plastering is measures in sq. m
striking is measures in sq. m
explain: All surface-finishing works like pointing, plastering, and formwork striking are measured by area (m²).

q: 171. For 12 mm thick cement plastering 1 : 6 on 100 sq. m new brick work, the quantity of cement required is
explain: For 100 m² of 12mm plaster, dry volume is calculated (adding for joints/wastage) and divided by the mix ratio (1+6).

q: 172. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1 : 2 : 4) 4 cm thick floor, the quantity of cement required is
explain: The wet volume is 4 m³. Applying a 1.52 factor for dry volume and dividing by 7 (ratio sum) yields approximately 0.94 m³.

q: 173. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm is
explain: Surface excavation or 'surface dressing' not exceeding 30 cm in depth is measured in square meters (m²).

q: 174. The unit of measurement for concrete work in R.C.C. is in
explain: Reinforced Cement Concrete (R.C.C.) work is a volumetric measurement carried out in cubic meters (cu m).

q: 175. The unit of measurement for wood work in door and window frame, rafters, beams, roof trusses etc is in
explain: Structural woodwork like frames (chaukhats), beams, and rafters is measured by volume in cubic meters (cu m).

q: 176. The unit of measurement for steel works in trusses and its parts is in
explain: Structural steel work in trusses, gusset plates, and rivets is generally measured by weight in quintals (100 kg).

q: 177. The unit of measurement for electric wiring or electrification light, fan, plug points is
explain: Internal electrical wiring is usually estimated per 'point' (e.g., one light point, one fan point).

q: 178. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: Rock excavation, including the labor for blasting and stacking the spoils, is measured by volume (cu m).

q: 179. The unit of payment for road side brick edging is in
explain: Edging or curbing work along roads is measured by the linear length in meters.

q: 180. Generally the unit of measurement for partition wall is
explain: Thin walls like half-brick partition walls are measured by area (sq. m) rather than volume.

q: 181. The unit of payment for AC sheet roofing is in
explain: Roofing materials like Asbestos Cement (AC) sheets are measured by the net area covered (sq. m).

q: 182. The quantity of stone required to produce 10 m³ of rubble stone masonry will be
explain: Due to voids and irregular shapes in rubble masonry, roughly 25% extra stone volume is required (12.5 m³ for 10 m³ masonry).

q: 183. The quantity of lime required for one coat of whitewashing of plastered surface of 100 m² will be
explain: Standard norms suggest approximately 10 kg of unslaked lime is needed for a single coat on 100 m² of surface.

q: 184. Which of the following comes under general overhead?
explain: General overheads include office expenses, staff salaries, and travelling expenses that cannot be attributed to a specific item.

q: 185. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. specified lead is
explain: The standard lead (horizontal distance) for earthwork excavation included in the base rate is 30 meters.

q: 186. While mixing cement mortar by volume, the volume of a cement bag is specified as
explain: A standard 50 kg bag of cement has a loose volume of approximately 0.035 cubic meters or 35 liters.

q: 187. In general for analysis of rates the reduction in volume of wet mixed mortar over the sum total volume of ingredient material is taken as
explain: When water is added to dry ingredients, the volume shrinks by about 25% due to voids being filled.

q: 188. In measuring form work no deduction is made for opening upto
explain: Very small openings (up to 0.01 m²) are ignored in formwork calculations to simplify the estimation.

q: 189. The plinth area method is also known as
explain: The plinth area estimate is calculated by multiplying the area (in sq. ft or sq. m) by a rate, hence 'square rate method'.

q: 190. The two important types of specification commonly used are
explain: Specifications generally focus on the quality of Materials and the method of execution for each Item of work.

q: 191. The defect liability period in construction norms for rate analysis is
explain: The standard defect liability period (during which the contractor is responsible for repairs) is usually one year after completion.

q: 192. The chairman of material rate fixation committee is
explain: In the Nepalese administrative context, the Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the committee that fixes district rates.

q: 193. The rate analysis norms prepared by ministry of physical infrastructure and transport, government of Nepal includes
explain: Modern rate analysis norms include the three basic components: Labor, Material, and Equipment/Machinery.

q: 194. Which of the following has the least life?
explain: Paint is a surface finish that deteriorates much faster (usually 3-5 years) than structural elements or pavements.

q: 195. The life of paint is assumed to be
explain: In valuation and maintenance cycles, the functional life of standard paint is typically taken as 5 years.

q: 196. Carpet area does not include the area of
options: the walls along with doors and other openings
explain: Carpet area is the net usable floor area excluding walls, circulation areas (corridors), and sanitary blocks.

q: 197. The floor area included the area of the balcony up to
explain: Generally, 50% of the balcony area is counted towards the total floor area in building regulations.

q: 198. The order of booking dimensions is
explain: Dimensions are always recorded in the standard sequence: Length first, then Breadth (or width), and finally Height (or depth/thickness).

q: 199. The rate of payment is made for 100 cu m (per % cu m) in case of
explain: Bulk earthwork and rock excavation are often billed in units of 100 cubic meters (percent cubic meters).

q: 200. The brick work is not measured in cu m in case of
options: one or more than one brick wall
explain: While standard brickwork is measured in cu m, half-brick walls (or partition walls) are measured in sq. m.
